## Northwind Cycles - Q3 2026 Review

Operations team · Prepared for the board · 14 October 2026

## Summary of the quarter

Revenue reached £4.8 million in the third quarter, up 12% on the same quarter last year and 4% ahead of plan. Growth came almost entirely from the new Commuter e-bike range, which launched in July and sold 1,940 units against a target of 1,500. Sales of traditional road bikes fell 6%, continuing the trend seen since the start of the year.

Gross margin improved from 31% to 34% after the move to the new frame supplier in Porto. Freight costs stayed high, but the larger order sizes negotiated in June offset most of the increase.

## Results by region

| Region | Q2 revenue | Q3 revenue | Change |
| - | - | - | - |
| North | £1.32m | £1.51m | +14% |
| Midlands | £1.05m | £1.12m | +7% |
| South | £1.71m | £1.88m | +10% |
| Online | £0.24m | £0.29m | +21% |

The North region benefited from two new dealer partnerships in Leeds and Newcastle. Online sales grew fastest, helped by the trade-in scheme that launched in August.

## Customer service

Warranty claims rose to 2.1% of units sold, mostly battery connector faults on early Commuter bikes. A revised connector has been fitted to all bikes built since 2 September, and claims for those units are below 0.5%. Average response time for support tickets fell from 26 hours to 11 hours after the new booking system went

live.

## Risks

Battery cells come from a single supplier, and its lead time has grown from six to ten weeks. If it grows further, Commuter production could pause in December, during the busiest month of the year. A second supplier is being qualified, with first samples due in November.

The planned price increase of 3% in January may slow dealer orders in the first quarter. The sales team recommends announcing it in November so dealers can order at current prices.

## Decisions needed

The board is asked to approve three items: a £180,000 budget to qualify the second battery supplier, the January price increase of 3%, and hiring two additional service technicians for the North region.

## Next quarter

The target for Q4 is £5.3 million in revenue, with 2,400 Commuter units. The team will launch the cargo version of the Commuter at the London Cycle Show on 21 November and open a service centre in Bristol in December.
